stories.head: True Anomaly secures $190M Series C funding
stories.body: True Anomaly has raised $190 million in Series C funding, bringing its valuation to $1.6 billion. The investment underscores the growing demand for co-orbital security and space domain awareness, as the DoD continues to ramp up its interest in these areas. Investors are clearly betting that space security will be a lucrative market.
stories.soWhat: When defense budgets get serious about space, it's a good time to be in the co-orbital security business.

stories.head: Ariane 6 to launch 36 Amazon Leo satellites
stories.body: The upcoming Ariane 6 launch will carry 36 satellites for Amazon's low Earth orbit (LEO) broadband project, a significant milestone for the e-commerce giant. This mission, powered by upgraded boosters, marks a critical step in Amazon's quest to compete with established players like SpaceX and OneWeb. The launch is expected to take place in the coming months.
stories.soWhat: With Amazon entering the satellite broadband game, the competition is about to get a lot more interesting — and crowded.

stories.head: Palantir wins $480M extension for TITAN program
stories.body: Palantir Technologies has secured a $480 million extension on its TITAN ground station program, continuing its long-standing relationship with the U.S. government. This extension highlights Palantir's ability to navigate the complex world of defense contracting, where persistence often pays off. The company has proven that it can deliver value in the realm of data analytics for military applications.
stories.soWhat: In defense contracting, it's not just about the technology; it's about being the last one standing at the negotiating table.

watchlist.title: Keep an eye on SpaceX's valuation
watchlist.body: With SpaceX's secondary market valuation hitting $470 billion, investors will be watching for any signs of a public offering.

talent.statLabel: Job orders YoY · plus 2 starters per head, an 8-year first
talent.head: Demand has doubled. So has our hit rate.
talent.body: EVONA's job orders are up 2.0× year-over-year, and for the first time in our eight-year history we're placing two new starters per EVONA staff member. The first number says demand is real. The second says we're converting it, which in recruitment is the only number that actually matters. Growth is heaviest in Series B/C startups; primes are running flat. Compensation isn't the variable. The constraint is schedule risk in the primes: senior engineers leave Boeing, Lockheed, Northrop because they want to ship hardware before retirement.
